**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

Section 24 satisfies the ASSIGN preferred position on every material term, and does so in our favour:

- **§24.1 — Customer assignment:** Free assignment to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all/substantially all assets, with no Vendor consent required (prompt written notice and assignee assumption only). **§13.3** carries the same carve-out through to licence rights, so the M&A path is not undercut by the licence grant.
- **§24.2 — Vendor assignment:** Vendor needs our prior written consent to assign, delegate material performance, *or* transfer by change of control — the anti-avoidance limb we normally have to add. Consent is not unreasonably withheld only for a capable, financially sound assignee, and Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor.
- **§24.4 — Our change of control:** Expressly gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, plus a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes. This closes the walk-away trigger.
- **§24.3 — Residual assignments:** Symmetrical mutual consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

I also checked for back-door change-of-control or exit rights elsewhere. The only assignment-adjacent termination right is **§9.2** (insolvency/general assignment for creditors), which is mutual and expressly carves out a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance — so it cannot be used as a change-of-control exit against us.

No deviation to raise; nothing here should be reopened in negotiation, as any redline would risk trading away favourable terms.
